jobs.title: Foreman Carpenter
jobs.desc:
Company Description
Kendellen Construction is a Cork-based construction company delivering high-quality building and civil works across the Munster region for public and private sector clients. The company works with organisations such as the Health Service Executive (HSE), University College Cork (UCC), and local Education and Training Boards, as well as a broad range of commercial clients. Services include refurbishments and fit-outs, commercial and public sector upgrades, roofing and flooring works, civil works, and planned and reactive maintenance. Kendellen Construction emphasizes safe, efficient project delivery, clear communication, and strict compliance with quality and regulatory standards, particularly in live healthcare and educational environments. The company operates under ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 certified systems, reflecting a strong commitment to safety, risk management, and continuous improvement.
Role Description
The Foreman Carpenter is a full-time, on-site role based in Cork, responsible for supervising and carrying out carpentry works across a variety of construction and refurbishment projects. Day-to-day tasks include leading and coordinating site carpentry teams, reading and interpreting drawings, planning work sequences, and ensuring that all carpentry activities are completed safely, on time, and to specification. The role involves hands-on carpentry work, including structural framing, installation of doors, windows, flooring, and other finishes, as well as the effective use of hand and power tools. The Foreman Carpenter will monitor quality, support compliance with company safety procedures and regulations, communicate progress and issues to site management, and collaborate with other trades to minimize disruption in live environments.
Qualifications
Strong practical Carpentry skills with experience across both structural and finishing work.
Proficiency with Power Tools and Hand Tools, including safe operation and basic maintenance.
Experience in Framing, including reading plans and setting out structural elements accurately.
Capability in Finish Carpentry, including installation of trims, doors, windows, and detailed joinery.
Previous experience in a foreman or lead carpenter role on commercial, public sector, or refurbishment projects.
Solid understanding of construction site safety practices and relevant regulations; familiarity with ISO-based systems is an advantage.
Ability to supervise and motivate site teams, coordinate with other trades, and maintain clear communication with project managers.
Good problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to work to strict deadlines while maintaining quality standards.
Relevant trade qualification or apprenticeship in carpentry; additional certifications in site management or health and safety are beneficial.

jobs.title: Customer Assistant - Ballincollig Express
jobs.desc:
About the role
We pride ourselves on offering customers the biggest range of products around. And that's not just food, but everything from clothes and kettles to financial services.
But did you know we offer the biggest job opportunities too? With stores across the UK and Ireland, and a variety of roles, we are always looking for people who are as passionate about helping customers as we are.
Our Every Little Helps approach doesn't just apply to our customers. It's at the very heart of everything we do at work - and it's what makes us different. We believe in treating each other with respect, and everyone having the opportunity to get on. That's what makes Tesco such a great place to work.
Should you be successful in your application, your offer will be subject to and conditional upon you providing your bank account details before your agreed start date.
You will be responsible for
Always put the customer first and consider them in everything you do.
Get to know your customers and serve them with pride.
Help to ensure products and services are available for customers at all times.
Handle all products with care to maintain quality and ensure they reach the customer in the best condition.
Keep the shop floor and back areas clean and tidy at all times.
Using the training you receive, follow department routines and processes.
Follow all company policies and adhere to Health and Safety routines.
Whilst you will have a core role, you may be asked to support your colleagues by helping in other departments.
You will need
Able to give great, natural customer service by proactively smiling, greeting, acknowledging and helping customers.
Works hard for customers, your team and your department.
You are able to prioritise to ensure anything you do is right for our customers.
Adaptable and resilient to meet the ever changing demands of our business.
You must be able to follow instructions either verbal or written.
You are reliable and a good timekeeper.
You must be smart and tidy at all times.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren't limited to:
Competitive Salary
Bonus Scheme*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2nd Clubcard available.*
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That's why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/
How can I let Tesco know I need additional support?
Please let us know you need additional support by emailing tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.

European Tech Recruit are working closely with a leading semicon company, based in the county Cork area, who are looking for a talented
Physical Design Engineer
to join their team
.
In this role you will be part of a global team that will drive and execute on all phases of the complete physical implementation for the next generation of premium-tier SOCs in bleeding edge technologies.
Responsibilities as
Physical Design Engineer:
Working on the physical implementation from floorplan to GDS for high-speed complex designs with aggressive PPA targets.
Taking part in the research of innovative methodologies for pushing the PPA limits in physical design, including the development of scripts and flows.
Working with cross-functional teams on understanding the design in context of physical implementation, timing closure and power optimization.
Demonstrating good understanding of and conducts research on industry trends and innovations in physical design to ensure solutions and deliverables align with best practices.
Performing complex analyses using statistics and data predictions to track benchmarks and identify issues or areas for improvement.
Working across teams to align on important areas of PPA improvement and ensure targets are met; ensures designs are innovative and compatible with highest standards.
Requirements:
4+ years of relevant experience in Physical Design.
Knowledge of entire PD flow from netlist to GDS (Floorplanning, Power planning, Placement/CTS/Routing and corresponding optimization steps).
Good experience and knowledge of tools for physical design implementation in advanced technologies nodes (10nm and below).
Excellent understanding of STA and timing closure methodologies, including impact on congestion/routing/power.
Good understanding of power analysis and power integrity analysis.
Understanding of Physical Verification and DRC closure.
Expert in automation skills using Perl and TCL and able to develop/support flows related to physical design.
Good communication skills and ability & desire to work in a cross-functional team environment.
If this role is of any interest please apply directly on LinkedIn or send a copy of your CV to nh@eu-recruit.com.

Terminology databases

Taxonomies
Ontologies
Style guides
Language standards

jobs.title: Veterinary Surgeon - Small Animal
jobs.desc:
Sunbeam Veterinary Hospital, Kinsale Road, Cork
Part-Time, Permanent | 32 Hours per Week
Salary up to €42,000 per annum (equivalent to €52,500 FTE)
Start Date: October 2026 (flexible)
Join a Practice Where Relationships Matter
At Sunbeam Vets Kinsale Road, we believe great veterinary care starts with great relationships. We're looking for a Small Animal Veterinary Surgeon to join our friendly and dedicated team in a well-established first opinion practice that has become a trusted part of the local community.
This is a fantastic opportunity for a confident GP vet who enjoys building lasting client relationships, delivering excellent clinical care, and working as part of a close-knit, supportive team. Our clients are loyal, engaged, and genuinely value the continuity and personal approach that our practice provides.
You'll be joining a small, experienced team where every individual makes a real difference, with the backing and resources of the wider Sunbeam Veterinary Group when needed.
The Opportunity
This role offers an excellent balance of medicine, surgery, preventative healthcare, and client engagement. As a key member of the clinical team, you'll manage a varied caseload of first opinion small animal cases, providing high-quality care from initial consultation through to diagnosis, treatment, and ongoing case management.
You'll be comfortable independently working up medical cases, developing treatment plans, interpreting diagnostic results, and performing routine soft tissue surgeries. While more advanced and specialist procedures can be referred to our larger teams and referral services within the Sunbeam network, we are looking for a vet who is confident managing day-to-day GP veterinary work without close supervision.
The role also includes elements of sole charge, making it ideally suited to an experienced veterinary surgeon who enjoys autonomy while still benefiting from the support of a collaborative team environment.
An interest in exotic species would be welcomed but is not essential.
Who We're Looking For
We're seeking a well-rounded Small Animal GP Veterinary Surgeon who is passionate about delivering excellent patient care and building strong relationships with clients and colleagues alike.
To be successful in this role, you must be VCI registered and confident managing routine first opinion medical and surgical cases independently. This includes procedures such as dog and cat spays, lump removals, routine diagnostics, case workups, and ongoing medical management.
Due to the level of autonomy required, this position is not suitable for new graduates or veterinary surgeons who require close supervision, structured mentorship, or extensive clinical support. We are looking for someone who can confidently contribute from day one and thrive within a busy first opinion environment.
A Supportive Team with a Community Focus
Sunbeam Vets Kinsale Road is home to a small and experienced team consisting of two veterinary surgeons, two veterinary nurses, and a dedicated receptionist. Together, we've built a welcoming practice where teamwork, trust, and client care are at the heart of everything we do.
Many of our clients have been with us for years, creating a genuine community atmosphere and allowing our team to develop meaningful, long-term relationships with both pets and their owners.
As part of the wider Sunbeam Veterinary Group, you'll also have access to the expertise, facilities, and support of a larger network including clinics in Blackpool, Cobh, and Passage West, as well as our specialist referral and emergency services.
Modern Facilities with the Support of a Larger Network
Our Kinsale Road branch is well-equipped with digital radiography, dental radiography, ultrasound, and in-house diagnostic capabilities, enabling efficient and thorough patient care.
Across The Wider Sunbeam Group, We Offer
24/7 emergency and critical care with round-the-clock veterinary cover
A team of approximately 9 veterinary surgeons and 15 qualified veterinary nurses
In-house laboratory services
Soft tissue and orthopaedic surgery
Advanced diagnostic imaging
Dental services
Canine hydrotherapy and rehabilitation
Dedicated nurse-led clinics including weight management, dental care, puppy, and senior pet clinics
Life in Kinsale Road, Cork
Located on the south side of Cork City, Kinsale Road offers the perfect balance of city convenience and community charm. With excellent transport links, easy access to Cork city centre, Cork Airport, and some of Ireland's most beautiful coastal towns, it's a fantastic place to live and work.
The area combines the energy of a thriving city with the warmth of a local neighbourhood, creating an ideal environment for veterinary professionals who enjoy becoming a valued part of their local community.
Working Pattern
This is a permanent part-time position working 32 hours per week on a planned rota basis, with schedules provided in advance.
Shifts are typically worked between: Monday to Friday: 8:00am to 6:00pm
Weekend commitment includes: 1 in 4 Saturdays: 9:00am to 2:00pm, 1 in 8 Sundays: 8:00am to 7:00pm
Comprehensive Benefits Package (subject To Pro-rata)
We believe in investing in our people. In addition to a competitive salary and a long-term, stable role, you’ll benefit from:
Work Life Balance & Employee Wellbeing
22 days annual leave
Additional birthday leave
Paid maternity, paternity and adoption leave packages
Cycle to Work Scheme
Company Sick Pay
Bereavement Leave
Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)
Wellbeing Centre access
Career Development
€1300 annual CPD allowance with 40 hours paid CPD leave
Full funding for any Certificates / Diplomas / PhD’s you may want to pursue
Opportunities for clinical and leadership progression
VCI and VDS memberships fully covered
Dedicated CARE fund - €1,100 annually to support exceptional cases
Additional Benefits
Annual Pay Reviews
Employer Pension Contributions
Discounted Veterinary Fees across the IVC Evidensia network
Free Flu Vaccinations
Access to “Pawesome” Benefits – retail and lifestyle discount platform
Opportunity to join company programmes (LGBTQ+, Wellbeing Champions, Nurses Committee, Clinical Board and many more)
Ready to Join Us?
If you're an experienced Small Animal Veterinary Surgeon looking for a role where you can enjoy genuine clinical autonomy, build lasting client relationships, and become part of a welcoming and supportive team, we'd love to hear from you.
Join Sunbeam Vets Kinsale Road and become part of a practice where exceptional patient care and strong community connections go hand in hand.

Job Title

Onsite – Carrigaline, IE
Job Specification:
Facilities Maintenance Caretaker
Job Title:
Facilities Maintenance Caretake / Maintenance Operative
Department:
Facilities
Reporting To:
FEHS Manager
Job Summary
The Maintenance Caretaker is responsible for the overall cleanliness, and physical upkeep of the property and its buildings. This role combines hands-on technical maintenance with daily operational duties to ensure a safe, functional, and welcoming environment for all staff and visitors.
Key Responsibilities
Conduct routine maintenance tasks across various areas, including:
Building Fabric: Handle minor carpentry, door hardware maintenance, office furniture adjustments, and paint touch-ups.
Plumbing: Basic repairs to taps, toilets, clear blockages.
Electrical (Non-Licensed): Assisting with basic electrical checks under supervision.
Grounds Maintenance: Outdoor Maintenance: Maintain external pathways, courtyards, and parking areas by weeding, clearing leaves and clearing litter.
Weather Response: Perform preventative gritting ahead of predicted cold snaps and snow clearing across entrances and driveways during adverse winter conditions.
Waste Coordination: Monitor the central bin areas, arrange for proper waste disposal, and ensure bottle/cans return bin is emptied frequently.
Contractor Liaison: Assist in gathering quotes and escorting external trade professionals for repairs sitewide, issuing the permit to work and ensuring the facility is safe to return to use after works.
Digital Literacy: Ability to use facility management systems, log maintenance tickets electronically, and respond to email queries.
Help maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, including work completed and materials used.
Adhere strictly to all company Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) policies and procedures, including proper use of PPE and safe working practices.
Maintain a high standard of housekeeping in all work areas.
Undertake any other duties as reasonably requested by the FEHS Manager Facilities Lead or Senior Maintenance Technician.
Qualifications & Experience
Education: Leaving Certificate or equivalent. Experience in a trade or a facilities role is an advantage.
Experience: Previous experience in a maintenance role, general labour, or similar practical work environment is preferred.
Driving Licence: A full, clean Irish driving licence is required as the role may involve collecting supplies.
Skills & Attributes
Practical Aptitude: Experience in the use of hand and power tools is required.
Physical Stamina: Capable of performing physical tasks, including lifting, carrying, bending, and standing for extended periods.
Problem-Solving: Basic ability to identify and report issues accurately.
Teamwork: A strong team player, willing to follow instructions and work cooperatively with others as well as on own initiative.
Communication: Good verbal communication skills to liaise with colleagues and report information clearly.
Reliability & Punctuality: Dependable and committed to consistent attendance and punctuality is essential.
Safety Conscious: A strong commitment to health and safety is imperative for the role.
Working Conditions
The role involves working both indoors and outdoors in various weather conditions.
Working at heights e.g., on ladders, MEWPs or roofs.
Exposure to various noise levels, dust, and common maintenance materials.
Typical working hours are 07:30 - 16:30 Monday to Friday, flexibility is required for urgent repairs or planned maintenance activities outside normal working hours like late evenings/weekends.

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills

Be part of the bigger picture and apply today.

Reporting to the Regional Controlling Manager, the

will join our European accounting team and provide support to the accounting and finance department by managing daily accounting tasks. Preparation of journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, and filing of periodic statutory returns will be the core part of this role.
It is an exciting time to join the Company as we will be implementing a new and improved ERP system (Oracle Fusion) in 2027 and the successful candidate will also be a part of this exciting implementation. As part of Veralto, a global Fortune 500 organization, there will be unlimited opportunities for growth, experiences and training.

Wroclaw, Berlin or Cork
and will be
hybrid
.
In this role, a typical day will look like:
Take ownership of the month-end and year end close process, ensuring accurate and timely completion of all financial reporting activities.
Prepare journal entries, reconciliations, and variance analysis to ensure the integrity of financial results.
Coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure all accounting transactions are captured correctly.
Ensure all balance sheet accounts are properly reconciled and all supporting documentation is complete and accurate.
Assist with internal and external audits, providing necessary documentation and support as required.
Coordination of income tax returns with external provider and ensuring all payments are made on time

Work closely with HR and our payroll provider to ensure that payroll entries are timely, accurate, and in line with company policies.
Prepare accounting transactions for multiple regions, ensuring adherence to both local accounting standards and global company policies.
Proactively recommend improvements to accounting processes and internal controls to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
Preparation and submission of periodic Vat, Vies, Intrastat and Statistical returns.
Comfortable working in a global matrix organization with the ability to build and leverage networks within an organization is desired

Qualified Accountant (E.g. ACA)
Knowledge of maintaining Local and US GAAP accounting ledgers
Excellent skills in MS Excel
Good understanding of both written and spoken English
Familiarity with ERP systems, particularly Oracle would be an advantage
Strong organisational and analytical capabilities with attention to detail, high levels of integrity, and professionalism at all times, with a proven ability to multi-task
Ability to work on own initiative and also as part of a global team
Enthusiastic, committed self-starter with proactive approach to problem solving

Electronic Design Engineer

Teamleader, DCS
Work Schedule

Job Summary
Reporting to a technical team leader, the engineer selected will be working as a part of a project team in an EN9100 environment, carrying out design and development activities on Moog’s motor controller products.
Primary Tasks & Responsibilities
Design & development of hardware (analog, digital and power electronics) for Moog’s range of servo-drive products whilst ensuring that the products:-
meet performance specifications, cost & reliability targets
comply with regulatory standards
are designed for manufacture & test (DFM &DFT)

The successful candidate will be expected to participate in design reviews and business reviews as required.
The successful candidate will be expected to work towards achieving defined project goals/milestones within tight project schedules.
The successful candidate will be expected to support a reasonable level of travel including on-site customer support.

Design team member in an ISO9OO1/AS9100D environment.
Maintain an up-to-date knowledge/expertise in the current state of the art.
Required Education
Minimum 2nd Class (Hons) degree or equivalent in an electronics / electrical engineering course.
Required Skills
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Excellent mathematical and analytical skills, problem identification, analysis and problem solving abilities.
Results oriented and deadline driven with a high degree of accountability, commitment and responsibility. Ability to produce very high quality results under tight time constraints.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills to interact with senior customers, management and team members.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Additional Skills – Advantageous
Knowledge of the operation and control of permanent magnet synchronous motors.
Knowledge of power conversion principles, topologies and technologies, and thermal management
Capability and experience in VHDL language.
Experience of hard real-time embedded system developments to defined project schedules.
Knowledge of electronic devices and FPGA communication with electronic devices (e.g. A/D, D/A, optical encoders).
Project Management

jobs.title: One Year Management Placement / Internship – Cork
jobs.desc:
Overview
We’re Enterprise Mobility. A family-owned, global mobility leader with a $39 billion turnover, nearly 90,000 team members, and operations in 95 countries. Led by CEO Chrissy Taylor, the third generation of the Taylor family, we’re built on a legacy that gives us the stability to focus on the long-term success of our people, our customers and our business.
Why join the One Year Management Placement Programme?
As an Intern, you’ll play a vital role in the success of Enterprise Mobility and receive a comprehensive introduction to our Graduate Management Training Programme. You'll gain valuable, real world business experience that can set you apart when you enter the job market.
From day one, we’ll invest in you. Based in one of our retail branches you’ll take on real responsibilities and gain hands-on experience across customer service, sales, marketing, finance, operations, and more - all within a supportive environment.
We work hard and reward hard work
You’ll be tackling the same challenges as those on our Graduate Management Training Programme, so it’s only fair you enjoy the same benefits. This is a paid position, with opportunities for promotion, performance bonuses, incentives, and employee referral rewards.
Award-winning training and development
Whether you’re building on existing skills or developing new ones, your growth is our priority. Through classroom learning, on-the-job training, and mentorship, you’ll have the tools and support to take the that first step in your career – and the one after that.
Our doors are open
As an Intern, your experience at Enterprise Mobility will be as unique as you because you shape who we are as much as we shape your skills, path and potential. We pride ourselves on opening our doors to a variety of voices, giving way to an experience that’s both inclusive and that inspires diversity of thought.
Responsibilities
You’ll have the chance to apply what you already know, while building a powerful set of hard and soft skills that you might not have expected. You’ll develop skills in:
Customer Service:
deliver exceptional experiences by confidently handling reservations, resolving enquiries, and building rapport with a diverse range of customers.
Sales and Marketing:
connect with local business partners, grow your network and develop lasting relationships.
Financial Control and Profitability:
understand the financial mechanics of a successful business, including cost control and interpreting profit and loss statements.
Operations and Logistics:
learn how to manage a fleet, plan strategically, and drive performance.
Leadership and Development:
Take the lead in mentoring, training, and developing your own team - with the opportunity to manage and promote others as you grow
Qualifications
We accept applications for our Management Placement and Internship Programme from all undergraduate university students regardless of university attended and subjects being studied. Our assessment is based on how you perform against our competencies and will judge you on that alone.
You must have a full manual Republic of Ireland, UK or EU driving licence, but we do make accommodations for applicants who don’t drive due to a disability.
No drug or alcohol related offence on driving record within the last five years is permitted.
Additional Information
Please let us know about any accommodations you may need to participate in our recruitment process.
Please limit your application to only one job posting based on where you live and/or plan to work. Applying to multiple locations will delay your application being processed.
This job posting is for applications within the following locations: Cork

jobs.desc:
Role Summary
We are seeking an innovative and technically minded Globalization Engineer (Language Specialist) to join our Globalization Engineering team.
This role combines deep linguistic expertise with technology, automation, AI innovation, and process optimization to help deliver exceptional multilingual customer experiences across global markets. The successful candidate will play a critical role in driving AI adoption, redesigning localization workflows & Quality Processes, automating manual processes, managing linguistic assets, and ensuring the highest standards of language quality across products, content, and customer-facing experiences.
This position is ideal for an individual who is passionate about languages, technology, artificial intelligence, and operational excellence, and who wants to help shape the future of AI-enabled localization and globalization.
This is a Hybrid position located in Ireland. You may be required to be onsite on an as-needed basis. We are only considering candidates in Ireland and are not offering relocation assistance at this time.
Position Details
About The Role
AI, Automation & Innovation
Drive the adoption of AI-powered localization technologies and workflows.
Identify opportunities to leverage Generative AI, Machine Translation, Large Language Models (LLMs), and automation technologies to improve scalability, quality, and efficiency.
Evaluate emerging AI solutions and recommend innovative approaches to improve multilingual customer experiences.
Design and implement process improvements that reduce manual effort and accelerate delivery.
Develop and support automation solutions using scripting, integrations, and workflow technologies.
Contribute to the evolution of AI-enabled globalization and localization engineering practices.

Taxonomies
Ontologies
Style guides
Language standards

Native or near-native proficiency in at least one of these languages - Italian / German / French / Dutch/ Brazilian / Portuguese.
Strong linguistic expertise and understanding of localization best practices.
Experience working in localization engineering, Localization QA, language technology, globalization, content operations, or a related field.

Prompt engineering experience.

Experience working with REST APIs and system integrations.

Understanding of Internationalization (i18n) principles and experience in guiding development best practice.

Experience supporting multilingual AI systems and language data management initiatives.

A passion for languages and linguistic quality.
Technically minded with a Curiosity and enthusiasm for AI and emerging technologies.
Strong technical aptitude and systems thinking.
Analytical and data-driven decision making.
Continuous improvement mindset.
Innovation and problem-solving capability.

jobs.title: Tier 2 Technical Customer Support Associate (German speaker), Amazon Leo
jobs.desc:
Description
Amazon Leo is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon Leo will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.
At Amazon Leo, our Technical Customer Support Associates (TCSA) deliver timely, accurate, and professional general and technical support to all Amazon Leo customers. The Amazon Leo Customer Support (CS) team is looking for driven individuals who are up to the challenge of solving customer issues while providing positive customer experience. TCSA are technically savvy problem-solvers with a focus on customer account security. An ideal candidate would be an excellent listener, handle change easily, be a quick learner and critical thinker, and be able to handle ambiguity. The position requires the ability to communicate professionally, with maturity and self-confidence, in German/French and English.
Shifts are assigned on a rotational basis and may include early mornings, evenings, overnights, weekends and public holidays. You will be required to work all shift patterns.
This position may require access to export-controlled information (ECI) subject to EAR and ITAR. Final employment decision is contingent upon satisfactory completion of export control screenings and obtaining any necessary export licenses or approvals, based on nationality, citizenship, and other factors considered by applicable export control regulations
Key job responsibilities
Receive and manage customer escalations from Tier 1 support, delivering timely and effective resolutions across phone, email, and chat channels.
Offer detailed technical support with clear and professional communication
Collaborate with other customer support teams to resolve complex issues
Document steps and resolutions in a clear, easy-to-follow format
Identify trends in customer issues and propose improvements to support processes
Help create knowledge base articles and team documentation
Stay current on new Amazon Leo products and features
A day in the life
As a Tier 2 Technical Support Associate, you'll be at the heart of our global connectivity mission. Your day will be dynamic, and purpose driven. You'll engage with customers, troubleshoot intricate technical issues, and collaborate with leadership and cross-functional teams to ensure seamless service delivery. Each interaction is an opportunity to make a tangible difference in someone's ability to connect, learn, and grow.
About The Team
Amazon Leo Global Operations is part of the Worldwide Consumer team. Our mission is to plan, develop and execute strategies to launch and operate Amazon Leo services globally through multiple distribution channels. Our team fosters a collaborative environment where you will work with regional and local operations to develop business models, partnerships, and fixed service operations.
Basic Qualifications
High school diploma, or equivalent
Experience using strong customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills
Experience communicating technical details verbally and in writing
Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
Knowledge of Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, SharePoint, and PowerPoint)
Speak, write, and read fluently in German
Understanding of internet technologies and ability to demonstrate knowledge by completing a required technical assessment
Strong problem-solving skills with a drive to dig into the details of systems and processes to resolve customer issues
Excellent communication skills and ability to convey insights from complex analyses to internal and end customers
Technical curiosity and enthusiasm for learning new technologies and helping customers succeed
Preferred Qualifications
Experience working in a fast-paced, rapidly changing operations environment
Experience in direct to consumer or business ISP and/or Satellite technical support
Experience working directly with end customers to resolve technical issues related to internet service, network connectivity, or end customer equipment
Fluency in multiple languages is a plus

The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. This pioneering spirit continues to guide us today as we innovate and expand, push beyond the boundaries of our industry, and shape its future. jobs.desc:
STA Design Engineer - ASIC / Low Power
We are partnered with a global leader in semiconductors and wireless technology focused on developing high-performance, low-power ASIC solutions for advanced cores and SOCs (System-on-Chips). The team are looking to hire an STA Engineer to take responsibility for conducting complex timing signoff activities and drive closure for next-generation products.
This is a permanent working opportunity based in Cork, Ireland.
Key responsibilities for this STA Design Engineer position:
Perform Static Timing Analysis (STA) and drive timing closure for complex cores and full-chip SOCs (e.g., in the Snapdragon family).
Evaluate block-level and top-level timing on gate-level PNR netlists.
Provide critical feedback to the RTL, Synthesis, and Physical Design teams to improve Power, Performance, and Area (PPA).
Create and execute Timing Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) to resolve critical timing violations.
Enhance techniques and methodologies for timing closure and STA flow accuracy to reduce turnaround time (TAT).
Develop automation scripts (Python, TCL, or Perl) for timing/power data mining and processing.
Key requirements:
4+ years of related work experience in Static Timing Analysis.
Expert proficiency in STA tools such as PrimeTime, PrimeShield, or Tempus for hierarchical analysis in large SoCs.
Hands-on experience with ECO tools (e.g., Tweaker, PrimeClosure, PTECO, Tempus ECO) for timing closure.
Highly proficient in automation scripting using Python, TCL, or Perl.
Strong knowledge of the complete ASIC design flow (RTL-to-GDS).
Keywords:
STA Design Engineer / Static Timing Analysis / STA / Timing Closure / ASIC Design / SOC / PrimeTime / Tempus / Timing ECO / PPA Optimization / Gate-Level Netlist / Python / TCL / Physical Design / RTL / Synthesis / Semiconductor / High-Performance Cores

We are looking for a hydrogeologist to join our team and work at the forefront of managing the challenges of providing resilient and environmentally sustainable water supplies for the future, while ensuring groundwater habitats are protected from new infrastructure development. We are undertaking an increasing number and range of important and exciting projects that involve groundwater resource evaluation, determining 'zone of contribution', and assessing the Environmental impacts on groundwater of new infrastructure. We are working for Group Water Schemes, Uisce Éireann, EirGrid, daa and government regulators. Building on this success, we are growing our team, and this growth could include you. You could help us to win and deliver work across our extensive client portfolio and enhance our reputation for excellence.

You will work closely with our technical specialists who are based in our established teams across Ireland and the UK. We have a friendly and approachable team with a strong reputation for delivering excellence with multiple clients.

Win, deliver and manage a portfolio of hydrogeology projects.
Develop trusted client relationships.
Champion high standards of performance, and influence project development.
Undertake work to a high standard, ensuring accuracy and quality.
Undertake and delegate complex problem solving, data gathering, processing, calculations, modelling and conceptualisation.
Write high quality reports and impact assessment.
Undertake proposal writing and costing.
Work closely with other hydrogeologists, sometimes delegating to, reviewing the work of and mentoring more junior staff.
Work collaboratively with other technical disciplines.
About You
A degree in science, engineering or mathematics.
Relevant years of work experience.
Demonstrable experience within consultancy, water company, regulator or academic fields.
Experience of water resources / hydrogeology.
Understanding links between surface and groundwater, abstraction, flooding and low flows.
Knowledge of the Water Framework Directive.
Experience of assessing and managing groundwater quality issues.
Experience of contaminated land and relation to groundwater.
Experience of preparing hydrogeology sections for EIAR Water Chapters.
Experience of WFD screening, scoping and assessment reports.
Knowledge of the operational and environmental regulatory framework of water management in Ireland.
A good understanding of hydrogeology, groundwater and aquifers, and in particular the karstic systems, common in Ireland.
You will have valid full, clean Irish driving licence.

Chartered or on the way to getting Chartered.
Experience of determining Zone of Contribution.

jobs.title: Customer Assistant - Macroom
jobs.desc:
Summary
From our Head Office to the shop floor and everywhere in between our primary goal is to create and deliver a fantastic customer journey for everyone who shops at Lidl.
Customer obsessed, high energy and love learning every day?
If that sounds like you, earn €460+ per week as a Customer Assistant on our standard 30 hour contract.
You’ll work across different shift times, on varied tasks and with different colleagues.
What does a normal day* as a Customer Assistant look like? (*there’s no such thing as ‘normal’ in retail but we’ve tried our best!)
As a Customer Assistant you are required to sell alcohol, therefore you must be 18 or over to work in our store.

A can-do attitude and excellent customer service skills

Who We Are
FedEx is the largest express transportation company in the world, connecting more than 220 countries and territories. We work every moment to deliver the most important package of someone’s day. Our team of passionate people know their day-to-day work is invaluable in delivering outstanding experience to our customers. 530,000 team members strong, we are as diverse as the world we serve. We love what we do, and we do it well. Our reach is big, and so are our dreams. Join us and let's write our next chapter together.
What You Will Be Doing

What Do We Offer

Extensive learning resources to further develop your skills and knowledge
Tuition Assistance Program (*applicable for FedEx positions with a permanent contract)
Employee Assistance Program for you and your family in difficult life situations
Employee reduced-rate shipping
Great career opportunities
FedEx is one of the worlds most admired companies and trusted brands year after year
Bring your ideas, individuality, and dreams to our global community. Feel good about where you work. Choose your career path - we’re ready to invest in your development. Join FedEx.
Diversity & Inclusion is more than the workplace. It’s the cultures we celebrate, the dreams we inspire, and creating a global community where everyone is accepted. At FedEx, diversity and inclusion happens because we do it together.
FedEx in the UK is Disability Confident ‘Committed’.
FedEx was built on a philosophy that puts people first, one we take seriously. We are an equal opportunity employer and we are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce in which we provide growth opportunities for all
Our Company
FedEx is one of the world's largest express transportation companies and has consistently been selected as one of the top 10 World’s Most Admired Companies by "Fortune" magazine. Every day FedEx delivers for its customers with transportation and business solutions, serving more than 220 countries and territories around the globe. We can serve this global network due to our outstanding team of FedEx team members, who are tasked with making every FedEx experience outstanding.
Our Philosophy
The People-Service-Profit philosophy (P-S-P) describes the principles that govern every FedEx decision, policy or activity. FedEx takes care of our people; they, in turn, deliver the impeccable service demanded by our customers, who reward us with the profitability necessary to secure our future. The essential element in making the People-Service-Profit philosophy such a positive force for the company is where we close the circle, and return these profits back into the business, and invest back in our people. Our success in the industry is attributed to our people. Through our P-S-P philosophy, we have a work environment that encourages team members to be innovative in delivering the highest possible quality of service to our customers. We care for their well-being, and value their contributions to the company.
Our Culture
Our culture is important for many reasons, and we intentionally bring it to life through our behaviors, actions and activities in every part of the world. The FedEx culture and values have been a cornerstone of our success and growth since we began in the early 1970’s. While other companies can copy our systems, infrastructure and processes, our culture makes us unique and is often a differentiating factor as we compete and grow in today’s global marketplace.
Equality, Opportunity & Diversity (EO&D)
Our greatest asset at FedEx is our people. We are committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive workforce, and offer equal opportunities, fairness, and respect to all regardless of who you are. We encourage you to apply even if you feel your experience does not align with all aspects in the job description as you could be exactly who we need for this or another opportunity.
We do not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on race, color, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, age, genetic information, citizenship, disability, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or any other characteristic protected under international and national laws and regulations. About the Role:
EPS Group has an immediate vacancy for an Electrical Engineer to join our Contracts team from our Mallow head office.
As part of our growing team, you will be responsible for the electrical engineering activities on Municipal and Industrial Wastewater Treatment Plants, Water Treatment Plants, various pumping stations and Data Centre Water Treatment Projects across Europe.
No two days will be the same, so your activities will vary and will be agreed with the Contracts Manager on an ongoing basis. You will support the design team through the process up to and including the onsite installation and commissioning phase.

Manage electrical aspects of projects and liaise with contractors and suppliers
Review the electrical installation with the BIM team to ensure the design is constructible and that there is adequate space for installation and maintenance of all equipment and cabling
Liaise with the design team & supply chain to ensure systems are compliant with specifications and drawings
Manage specialist vendors during the commissioning process to ensure timely completion of their works
Develop Site Instruction Packs, handover packs and test packs as required
Attending quality meetings and participate in QA/QC walk downs when required
Review and answer technical queries from site in relation to specifications/drawings/materials and equipment
Issue requisitions and ensure all materials delivered are as per specifications and submittals
Work with multi-disciplinary teams, including automation, mechanical, civil, and process engineers

Technical knowledge and experience of 3 phase industrial installations, specifically including 3 phase motors , starters, control panels, PLC's and associated instrumentation
Proficiency in reading and creating electrical schematics, P&IDs, and wiring diagrams
Experience with AutoCAD and Trimble for electrical design and layout
Strong technical knowledge of Safe Electric certification
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently or within a team
Ability to lead and take responsibility for project completion

Similar relevant third level qualification and experience will be considered

Opportunities for professional development and career growth

jobs.title: Veterinary Nurse
jobs.desc:
Veterinary Nurse - Small Animal
Acorn Veterinary Clinic, Mallow, Co. Cork
Part-Time | Permanent
24 Hours per Week | Flexible Working Arrangements Available
Join a Team You'll Love Being Part Of
At Acorn Vets, we believe that great veterinary care starts with a great team. We're looking for a friendly, adaptable and enthusiastic Veterinary Nurse to join our welcoming practice in Mallow, where teamwork, community, and patient care are at the heart of everything we do.
This is a fantastic opportunity for a nurse seeking genuine flexibility, clinical variety, and a positive working environment. Whether you're newly qualified and ready to begin your nursing career, or you're an experienced RVN looking for a role that offers a better work-life balance, we'd love to hear from you.
You'll be joining a close-knit and supportive team of vets, nurses, and support staff who genuinely enjoy working together and are passionate about providing exceptional care to both patients and clients. Every day brings something different, and you'll play a valued role in ensuring our patients receive the highest standard of veterinary care.
The Role: Flexible, Varied & Rewarding
This permanent part-time position offers 24 hours per week, with flexibility around how those hours are worked. We understand that everyone's circumstances are different and are happy to discuss working arrangements that suit both you and the practice.
Our clinic operates between 8:30am and 6:00pm, with shifts scheduled on a rota basis. The role also includes a 1 in 3 Saturday rota and participation in a minimal out-of-hours emergency on-call service. The commitment is exceptionally light, with nurses typically called out only around three times per year on average.
As a Veterinary Nurse at Acorn Vets, you'll enjoy a varied caseload and be actively involved in all aspects of practice life. You'll have the opportunity to utilise your nursing skills across surgical, medical and inpatient care while building strong relationships with clients and supporting them throughout their pets' healthcare journey.
Working closely with our experienced veterinary team, you'll be encouraged to contribute your ideas, continue developing your clinical skills, and take pride in providing outstanding patient care every day.
About Acorn Vets
Acorn Vets has proudly cared for animals and supported pet owners and farming communities throughout North Cork for many years. Our practice has built a trusted reputation through a combination of high-quality veterinary care, strong client relationships, and a genuine commitment to the communities we serve.
From much-loved family pets to farm animals, our team is passionate about delivering compassionate care and practical clinical solutions. We combine modern veterinary medicine with a friendly, community-focused approach that has kept clients returning to us for generations.
You'll be based in our Mallow practice, where you'll become part of a supportive and collaborative team environment. While we also have a sister site in Kildorrery, this position is based solely in Mallow and there is no expectation for regular travel between practices.
As part of the IVC Evidensia network, Acorn Vets benefits from access to industry-leading resources, professional development opportunities, and a wider support network, while maintaining the same local identity, close-knit culture, and trusted relationships that make the practice so special.
Why Mallow?
Located in the heart of North Cork, Mallow offers the perfect blend of town and country living. With excellent transport links to Cork City, beautiful countryside on your doorstep, and a thriving local community, it's an ideal location for those seeking a rewarding career without sacrificing quality of life.
The town is known for its welcoming atmosphere, strong sense of community, and easy access to some of Munster's most scenic locations, making it a fantastic place to live, work, and build lasting connections.
About You
We're looking for a Veterinary Nurse who is passionate about patient care and enjoys being part of a collaborative and supportive team.
You must be registered with the Veterinary Council of Ireland and committed to maintaining high clinical standards. Just as importantly, you'll be friendly, approachable, and enjoy building positive relationships with clients, colleagues, and patients alike.
We're seeking someone who is adaptable and flexible, enjoys a varied workload, and is happy working within a busy practice environment. Whether you're at the beginning of your career or bring years of nursing experience, you'll find support, encouragement, and opportunities to develop within our team.
Most importantly, we're looking for someone who will embrace our values, contribute positively to team culture, and share our passion for delivering exceptional veterinary care.
Comprehensive Benefits Package (subject To Pro-rata)
We believe in investing in our people. In addition to a competitive salary and a long-term, stable role, you’ll benefit from:

22 days annual leave (pro-rata)

Professional Memberships & Additional Benefits
VCI membership paid
VDS cover provided
Employer pension contributions
Annual salary reviews
Discounted veterinary care across the IVC Evidensia network
Access to Pawesome Benefits retail and lifestyle discounts
Free flu vaccinations

We’re Enterprise Mobility. A family-owned, global mobility leader with a $39 billion turnover, nearly 90,000 team members, and operations in 95 countries. Led by CEO Chrissy Taylor, the third generation of the Taylor family, we’re built on a legacy that gives us the stability to focus on the long-term success of our people, our customers and our business.
Why join the Graduate Management Training Programme?
As a Graduate Management Trainee, you'll have the freedom and support to explore your leadership potential - and the opportunity to become a branch manager in one of our retail operations in as little as two years. In fact, most of our senior leaders began their careers in this very role - including our current CEO.
From day one, we’ll invest in you. You’ll be in a supportive environment where you’ll take on real responsibilities and gain invaluable hands-on experience in customer service, sales, marketing, finance, operations, and more.
We work hard and reward hard work
Your work will be recognised with performance-based incentives and opportunities for continued promotion. Our unique promote-from-within culture means you can keep your career moving forward without having to change organisations.
Award-winning training and development
Whether you’re building on existing strengths or developing new ones, your growth is our priority. Through classroom learning, on-the-job training, and mentorship, you’ll have the tools and support to take the next step – and the one after that.
Our doors are open
As a Graduate Management Trainee, your experience at Enterprise Mobility will be as unique as you because you shape who we are as much as we shape your skills, path and potential. We pride ourselves on opening our doors to a variety of voices, giving way to an experience that’s both inclusive and that inspires diversity of thought.
Responsibilities

connect with local business partners, grow your network and develop lasting relationships.

learn how to manage a fleet, plan strategically, and drive performance.

take the lead in mentoring, training, and developing your own team - with the opportunity to manage and promote others as you grow.

jobs.title: Marsh Country Technology Leader – Ireland
jobs.desc:
What can you expect?
Marsh People and Investments (Marsh P&I) is the Health, Wealth and Career business of Marsh, a global professional services firm headquartered in New York. Ireland is one of Marsh P&I’s most strategically significant markets in Europe, and this role exists to bring clearer ownership stronger business partnership and greater value from the country’s technology investment.
This is an opportunity to shape how technology supports the market’s business, colleague and client priorities across a complex, distributed technology environment. As the single accountable technology leader for Ireland, you will translate business and client priorities into a clear, prioritised technology roadmap and ensure that regional, global, local, vendor and squad-based teams deliver against agreed outcomes.
You will be accountable for delivery performance, major capital investment programmes, investment prioritisation and operational stability. You will act as a genuine technology partner to the Country CEO, COO and business leaders, communicating complex technology issues clearly and ensuring that Ireland receives appropriate value from the technology investment attributed to it. The role reports into Regional Technology Leadership and has a formal dotted-line reporting relationship to the Country CEO, reflecting the role’s accountability for delivering technology outcomes in Ireland.
We will count on you to:
Define and maintain a single integrated country technology roadmap — covering strategic programmes, regulatory commitments, business demand, and operational resilience — and ensure it is funded, sequenced, and delivered.
Act as the primary technology partner to the Country CEO, COO, and business leaders, translating business priorities into technology decisions and communicating technology matters in clear commercial language.
Drive delivery accountability across regional, global, local, vendor, and squad-based teams, owning outcomes across a matrixed environment.
Lead governance and delivery oversight of major Capex programmes, from business case through to benefits realisation, with the authority to challenge or reprioritise when delivery or value is at risk.
Establish clear escalation routes and resolve cross-team delivery dependencies, acting as the primary escalation point for technology issues in the country.
Maintain service continuity and operational stability while identifying pragmatic opportunities for automation, data, and AI-enabled improvement.
Represent Marsh P&I Technology confidently with clients and senior stakeholders, supporting proposals, service reviews, client conversations, remediation activity and discussions about technology options, risks and investment.
What you need to have:
10+ years’ experience in technology, digital or business technology leadership, including at least five years operating at senior leadership level as a CIO, CTO, Technology Director, Head of Technology or equivalent.
Proven track record of leading complex technology programmes through to successful outcomes, managing scope, risk, dependencies, budget, timelines and benefits realisation.
Real experience in a matrixed model. Influencing without full authority, aligning distributed teams, and holding delivery partners accountable.
Strong Capex governance experience: business case development, investment approval, benefits tracking, and programme recovery.
The commercial credibility to engage at CEO and COO level, making complex technology decisions clear and decision-ready.
Broad understanding of technology operations, platforms, architecture, service management, cyber risk and operational resilience, with the ability to lead through subject-matter experts rather than needing to be the deepest technical specialist.
Background in financial services, professional services, or a similarly regulated, client-facing industry preferred.
What makes you stand out:
You've earned the trust of senior business stakeholders not just through technical knowledge, but by consistently connecting technology to what the business actually needs.
You lead with clarity in ambiguous, matrixed environments and you know how to hold teams accountable without direct authority.
You have the confidence to challenge commitments that are not ready, recommend a change of direction when a programme is not delivering, and stand behind well-reasoned decisions. Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to move comfortably between engineering teams and boardroom conversations.
You are commercially curious: you ask what technology is costing, what Ireland is receiving in return, and whether investment and resource allocations are delivering fair value.
Why join our team:
We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders.
We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can collaborate with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities.
Our scale enables a range of career opportunities, with visibility at regional and global leadership level across one of Marsh's key European markets.
Note this role is based in Marsh Ireland – Cork or Dublin – with an expectation of working from the office 3 days per week.
Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other less represented groups tend to only apply when they check every box. So, if you think you have what it takes, but don't necessarily meet every single point on what is needed, please still get in touch.

This permanent part-time position offers 24 hours per week, with flexibility around how those hours are worked. We understand that everyone's circumstances are different and are happy to discuss working arrangements that suit both you and the practice.
Our clinic operates between 8:30am and 6:00pm, with shifts scheduled on a rota basis. The role also includes a 1 in 3 Saturday rota and participation in a minimal out-of-hours emergency on-call service. Acorn Vets has proudly cared for animals and supported pet owners and farming communities throughout North Cork for many years. Our practice has built a trusted reputation through a combination of high-quality veterinary care, strong client relationships, and a genuine commitment to the communities we serve.
From much-loved family pets to farm animals, our team is passionate about delivering compassionate care and practical clinical solutions. We combine modern veterinary medicine with a friendly, community-focused approach that has kept clients returning to us for generations.
You'll be based in our Mallow practice, where you'll become part of a supportive and collaborative team environment. While we also have a sister site in Kildorrery, this position is based solely in Mallow and there is no expectation for regular travel between practices.

Why Mallow?
Located in the heart of North Cork, Mallow offers the perfect blend of town and country living. With excellent transport links to Cork City, beautiful countryside on your doorstep, and a thriving local community, it's an ideal location for those seeking a rewarding career without sacrificing quality of life.
The town is known for its welcoming atmosphere, strong sense of community, and easy access to some of Munster's most scenic locations, making it a fantastic place to live, work, and build lasting connections.

We're looking for a Veterinary Nurse who is passionate about patient care and enjoys being part of a collaborative and supportive team.
You must be registered with the Veterinary Council of Ireland and committed to maintaining high clinical standards. Just as importantly, you'll be friendly, approachable, and enjoy building positive relationships with clients, colleagues, and patients alike.
We're seeking someone who is adaptable and flexible, enjoys a varied workload, and is happy working within a busy practice environment. Whether you're at the beginning of your career or bring years of nursing experience, you'll find support, encouragement, and opportunities to develop within our team.
Most importantly, we're looking for someone who will embrace our values, contribute positively to team culture, and share our passion for delivering exceptional veterinary care.

Leadership Academy for aspiring Head Nurses and Practice Managers
Opportunities for clinical and professional progression across the IVC Evidensia network

VCI membership paid
VDS cover provided
Employer pension contributions
Annual salary reviews
Discounted veterinary care across the IVC Evidensia network
Access to Pawesome Benefits retail and lifestyle discounts
Free flu vaccinations

If you're looking for a role that offers flexibility, a genuinely supportive team, and the opportunity to make a real difference within a well-respected local practice, we'd love to hear from you.

plays a key role in the day‑to‑day delivery of clinical and administrative services within the clinic. This is a structured trainee position designed to develop individuals into a fully independent ophthalmic technician administrator through hands‑on training, competency‑based assessment and progressive responsibility.
Training & Progression
Structured onboarding and role‑specific training will be provided across both clinical and administrative functions.
Trainees will initially work under supervision, gradually progressing to independent responsibility as competence is demonstrated.
Once trained and assessed as competent, individuals will carry out duties independently in line with clinic standards.
Progression is based on competency, performance, reliability, and ability to manage responsibilities independently.

Clinical Duties

Carrying out patient pre‑screening and diagnostic testing, including: Visual acuity, Visual fields. Pupil checks, OCT, Biometry and Intraocular pressure testing.
Administering eye drops.
Taking accurate patient histories and supporting clinical assessments, ensuring documentation is complete, clear, and aligned with clinic standards.
Scribing during consultations (in person and remotely), accurately documenting clinical findings and consultant instructions.
Preparing patients for examinations and procedures to ensure a smooth and professional patient journey.
Maintaining clinical rooms and equipment to required standards.
Monitoring stock levels and supporting the management of clinical supplies.
Adhering to all clinical protocols, safety standards, infection control, and data protection requirements.
Maintaining strict patient confidentiality at all times.
Supporting end‑of‑day clinic close‑down processes.
Escalating patient concerns, incidents, or clinical risks promptly and appropriately.
Supporting patient education (explaining tests, next steps, and post‑operative instructions once trained).
Patient Flow & Clinic Support
Actively managing and prioritising patient flow within the clinic.
Identifying delays or bottlenecks and escalating issues where required.
Handling patient queries, concerns, or complaints in a professional and calm manner and escalating appropriately.
Ensuring patients are kept informed of delays and next steps.
Delivering a consistently high standard of patient experience throughout the clinic journey.
Supporting the smooth and efficient running of clinics by preparing in advance and anticipating requirements.
Working closely with consultants, technicians, and administrative staff to ensure clinics run to schedule.
Assisting with clinic set‑up and room preparation between sessions.
Administrative Duties
Managing and coordinating patient appointments across clinics through live scheduling.
Updating patient records accurately using practice management systems.
Supporting billing, insurance processing, and administrative workflows.
Communicating effectively with patients via phone and email.
Ensuring all documentation is completed accurately and in line with clinic standards.
Working to defined processes to ensure consistency, quality, and compliance.
Maintaining accurate records across both clinical and administrative systems.
Supporting audit and compliance requirements through accurate documentation.
Assisting with data quality checks and corrections where required.
Carrying out any other reasonable duties in line with the needs of the business.
Requirements
Ability to work in a fast‑paced, high‑volume clinical environment.
Willingness to provide cover across different clinic locations when required.
Ability to adapt quickly to different teams, consultants, and working styles.
Strong reliability, timekeeping, and attendance.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong IT skills and high accuracy in data entry.
Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise effectively.
Willingness to learn quickly and take ownership of responsibilities.
Confidence to ask questions and escalate concerns appropriately.
Flexible approach to work.

jobs.title: Network Security (WAF) Engineer
jobs.desc:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.
Network Security Engineer (WAF) – P3
About The Role (Job Summary)
As a Network Security Engineer (Web Application Firewall), you will play a key role in protecting McKesson’s global technology environment by designing, implementing, and optimising security controls across cloud and on-premises platforms. You will work closely with infrastructure, application, and cybersecurity teams to secure internet-facing applications, strengthen network security controls, and reduce organisational risk. This role combines hands-on engineering with security consulting, helping teams integrate security into technology solutions while maintaining application availability and performance. You will also contribute to incident response, risk reduction initiatives, and the continuous improvement of McKesson’s cybersecurity capabilities.
What You’ll Do (Responsibilities)
Design, implement, and maintain Web Application Firewall (WAF) protections for internet-facing applications, including custom security policies, rate limiting, geo-blocking, and threat detection rules.
Develop and manage network security controls, including firewall policies, network segmentation, ingress and egress controls, and secure access configurations.
Partner with application, infrastructure, and engineering teams to understand application architectures, traffic flows, and business requirements, ensuring security controls are both effective and operationally sustainable.
Analyse network traffic, security events, and application behaviour to identify risks, investigate security concerns, and improve detection capabilities.
Evaluate, implement, and optimise security technologies and controls to enhance protection against vulnerabilities, emerging threats, and unauthorised access.
Support incident response, forensic investigations, vulnerability remediation activities, and disaster recovery planning by providing technical security expertise.
Document security architectures, configurations, procedures, and standards while promoting security best practices across technology teams.
Basic Requirements
4+ years of experience implementing and supporting enterprise network security technologies, including firewalls, web application firewalls, or intrusion prevention systems.
Experience configuring and managing Web Application Firewall (WAF) solutions to protect internet-facing applications and APIs.
Experience designing, implementing, and maintaining firewall rules, network segmentation controls, and access management policies in enterprise environments.
Strong understanding of TCP/IP networking, application traffic flows, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, and network security architecture principles.
Experience analysing network traffic, security logs, and security events to support investigations, threat detection, and incident response activities.
Experience assessing security risks, validating security control effectiveness, and identifying opportunities to improve security posture.
Strong documentation skills with experience creating technical documentation, security standards, procedures, and configuration records.
Preferred Skills/Experience
Minimum Education & Typical Experience or Equivalent Combination: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience, with 4+ years of experience in cybersecurity engineering, network security, infrastructure security, or a related technical field.
Experience securing cloud-based environments and applications within AWS, Azure, or other enterprise cloud platforms.
Knowledge of Operational Technology (OT) security, supply chain security, or AI security risks and associated controls.
Experience mentoring team members and contributing to technical leadership, security best practices, and continuous improvement initiatives.
At McKesson, we care about the well-being of the patients and communities we serve, and that starts with caring for our people. That’s why we have a Total Rewards package that includes comprehensive benefits to support physical, mental, and financial well-being. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer / Process Engineer
jobs.desc:
Role Description
We are seeking technically minded and detail-oriented professionals for the positions of Manufacturing Engineer / Process Engineer. These roles focus on improving production systems, optimizing operational workflows, maintaining quality standards, and supporting efficient manufacturing operations. Successful candidates will contribute to process improvement initiatives, technical problem-solving, and the implementation of effective engineering solutions.
Manufacturing Engineers are responsible for developing, evaluating, and improving manufacturing methods, production equipment, and assembly processes. Key duties include analyzing production performance, identifying operational inefficiencies, coordinating equipment installations, optimizing resource utilization, and ensuring that manufacturing activities meet established quality and safety standards. They collaborate with production, quality, maintenance, and design teams to enhance productivity, reduce waste, and support the introduction of new products or technologies.
Process Engineers focus on analyzing, designing, and optimizing industrial processes to improve efficiency, consistency, and product quality. Responsibilities include reviewing process parameters, investigating production issues, identifying root causes, developing corrective actions, and implementing process control measures. They also support process validation, document technical procedures, monitor performance indicators, and recommend improvements that reduce operating costs and minimize material losses.
Both roles require strong analytical thinking, technical knowledge, and the ability to translate operational data into practical improvements. Professionals in these positions contribute to continuous improvement programs, equipment performance evaluations, production planning, and cross-functional projects while ensuring compliance with applicable technical specifications and operational standards.
Qualifications
Degree or diploma in Manufacturing Engineering, Process Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Understanding of manufacturing systems, production workflows, process optimization, and quality control principles.
Ability to analyze technical data, identify inefficiencies, and develop practical engineering solutions.
Familiarity with continuous improvement methodologies, such as Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or root cause analysis.
Knowledge of engineering drawings, technical specifications, process documentation, and standard operating procedures.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and the ability to work with production data, reports, and performance indicators.
Familiarity with CAD software, process simulation tools, statistical analysis software, or manufacturing systems is an advantage.
Strong problem-solving, organizational, communication, and teamwork skills.
Ability to coordinate with cross-functional teams and manage multiple technical tasks effectively.
Commitment to quality, operational efficiency, workplace safety, and continuous improvement.

While the role focuses on geotechnical engineering design and delivery, you will also gain valuable exposure to the full breadth of Ground Engineering disciplines. It also offers the opportunity to place sustainability at the heart of engineering solutions.

Deliver geotechnical design and analysis for foundations, retaining structures, slope stability, and earthworks on major international commissions (e.g., hyperscale data centres in Europe, the Fehmarnsund Link) and nationally significant Irish infrastructure (e.g., Metrolink, DART+, N6 Galway Ring Road).
Prepare high-quality design reports, technical specifications, desk studies, and site walkovers for educational, pharmaceutical, industrial, and commercial developments.
Plan, supervise, and interpret geotechnical ground investigations, providing technical support during the construction phase, including periodic site visits.
Incorporate the latest digital tools, automation, and numerical analysis into our projects to enhance project delivery.
Develop your project management and commercial awareness skills, while supporting and mentoring junior colleagues as you strengthen your own leadership capabilities.
